summary: the expectancy standard error behind every risk decision is taken across emission cohorts rather than across observations (Fama-MacBeth): sources emit their whole cross-section in one burst, so 23 simultaneous calls are one draw of the market and not 23 independent ones — the point estimate is the mean of cohort means, the standard error is sd(cohort means)/sqrt(B), and it is zero below two cohorts; measured 2.23x understatement on the live trend cohorts and reversion's entire positive reading is a single cross-section, so the gate no longer opens on evidence that does not exist (ADR-0077)
